condition: suspected acute pediatric postseptal orbital infection presenting with unilateral anterior globe protrusion after 4 days of nasal congestion
level_rationale: Acute forward bulging of the right eye developing today after 4 days of nasal congestion in an 8-year-old child indicates suspected postseptal orbital infection or subperiosteal orbital abscess with optic nerve and cavernous sinus risk requiring immediate hospital computed tomography imaging, intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics, and surgical consultation, whereas mild right eye watering when sneezing on day 4 of a stuffy nose reflects benign nasolacrimal congestion appropriate for home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain parent-carer lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-eye mild sneeze-tearing cold self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (8-year-old son, 4 days of nasal congestion, and acute forward bulging of his right eye today) with an exact 14-word vs 14-word span swap and zero diagnosis labels ('cellulitis', 'rhinitis', and 'sinusitis' omitted from prompt texts). Keeping f2 as 4-day nasal congestion and keeping 'his right eye' identical in f3 avoids stranding fever or proptosis and adds zero new body sites when f3 shifts under Rule A and Rule D to mild right-eye watering on sneezing (level 4 hospital to level 1 home self-care) with zero stated negatives.
